name: ARMENIA
lead: Armenia is one of the world's oldest nations. It is landlocked in the Caucasus, where Europe meets Asia. In 301 AD it became the first country to adopt Christianity. Old monasteries cling to cliffsides. Armenians have kept their own alphabet alive for 1,600 years.
geo: Mountains cover almost all of Armenia. The average height is about 1,800 metres, higher than Switzerland's average. Georgia, Azerbaijan, Iran, and Turkey border it. It has no sea coast.
Lake Sevan lies 1,900 metres above sea level, one of the world's largest high-altitude lakes. It sparkles blue among golden hills. Swimmers love it despite the chilly water.
animals: The Armenian mouflon, a wild mountain sheep with huge curved horns, roams the rocky south. Brown bears and lynx live in the northern forests around Dilijan.
Lake Sevan holds the ishkhan, a trout found nowhere else on Earth. Griffon vultures and golden eagles soar above ancient monasteries.
culture: Armenia invented its own 38-letter alphabet in 405 AD. It looks like no other script. Alphabet Park in Yerevan has giant stone letters that children love to climb.
Lavash flatbread bakes in a clay tonir oven sunk into the ground. UNESCO lists it as heritage food. Apricots are the national fruit. The Latin word 'armeniaca' means 'from Armenia'.
history: In 301 AD, King Tiridates III made Christianity the state religion. Armenia was the first nation ever to do this. Monasteries like Geghard are carved into solid rock.
Persians, Byzantines, Arabs, and Ottomans ruled Armenia for centuries. In 1991, Armenians voted for independence after 70 years in the Soviet Union. They raised their red-blue-orange flag again.
wows: Yerevan is the 'Pink City', built from rosy volcanic stone called tuff.
An Armenian cave in 2008 held the world's oldest leather shoe, 5,500 years old.
A 6,100-year-old winery was found near Areni village.
The alphabet is nearly unchanged after 1,600 years.
Yerevan's Cascade staircase has 572 steps and a hidden escalator inside.
Armenian children must study chess at school from age seven.
Tatev's 5.7 km tramway is the world's longest non-stop cable car.

myths.fact: They call it Hayastan. Armenia is the name other peoples gave it.
Ararat is inside Turkey, and has been since 1921. Armenia's coat of arms still shows it.
